title: Design and Integration of Chassis and Power-train for a Range Extended Electric Vehicle
summary: A two-seater academic REEV study connecting electric propulsion with an engine-generator range extender. FYP-1 established the architecture and integration methodology.
overview: Range anxiety and limited charging access motivate this two-seater academic project at Air University. The selected series architecture keeps the wheels electrically driven: the battery supplies a controller and traction motor, while a petrol engine runs a generator to support or recharge the electrical system when required. The engine has no direct mechanical connection to the wheels.
approach: Compared battery-electric, hybrid and range-extended concepts through a literature review, then selected a series architecture for the proposed two-seater.

Defined the traction path as battery/DC bus → motor controller → electric motor → final drive and wheels. The engine-generator branch supplies electrical energy to the DC bus or battery; there is no mechanical engine-to-wheel path.
Identified the battery, traction motor, controller, petrol engine, generator, fuel tank and DC/DC converter, relating selection to voltage, current, torque and auxiliary-load requirements.

Set out a sizing method using vehicle mass, speed, acceleration and wheel radius for traction requirements, followed by battery voltage, current and energy-capacity considerations. Final compatible values remain later-phase work.

Defined integration and evaluation methodology around motor operation, battery support and generator charging response, with a conceptual state-of-charge flowchart for electric and generator-supported modes.
components: Petrol engine and generator range extender
DC/DC converter for auxiliary electrical loads
outcomes: FYP-1 completed the literature review, architecture selection, component identification and sizing/integration methodology.
The block diagram and state-of-charge flowchart explain the proposed energy and control paths. The vehicle rendering communicates the concept, not completed construction.
No achieved driving range, finalized component ratings or completed vehicle demonstration is claimed.

evidenceNotes: Prefer team spelling in the matching P 2348.docx report over presentation variants.
Older single-seater, vehicle-conversion and component-sizing files represent conflicting proposal scenarios; exact mass, rating, cost and range figures are excluded.
Owner phase boundaries take precedence over inconsistent completed-tense methodology sentences in report.
problem: How can a small two-seater vehicle retain electric propulsion while reducing dependence on charging access and a very large battery pack?
context: Air University final-year team project. FYP-1 is complete; chassis and power-train development continues in later academic phases.
constraints: Battery, motor, controller and generator choices must form a compatible electrical system; the current deliverable establishes the selection method rather than a final hardware specification.
The project concerns component selection and integration. Manufacturing an engine, generator or traction motor is outside its stated scope.
The engine-generator range extender uses petrol, so the architecture is not a zero-emission vehicle claim.
lessons: A series architecture separates mechanical propulsion from the range extender: both energy sources support one electric traction path.
Component sizing and integration must be considered together, rather than selecting a motor, battery and generator independently.
nextSteps: FYP-2: carry out the design calculations and component sizing for the selected two-seater scenario.
FYP-3: develop the planned final vehicle, integrating the chassis and power-train and documenting its operation.
